clue.text: Vow made by page left on one side

parts.note: an edge is a side or border of something

explanation.surface: Someone swears an oath, then a page boy wanders off to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn promise, the same thing as a vow.

clue.text: A director's tip

definitions.meaning: something that directs or shows the way, like a needle on a dial
a hint or piece of advice

explanation.surface: Advice given by a film director.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is both an indicator that directs and a useful hint.

clue.text: Over 50, still making a stand

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: to still is to calm or soothe, which is to ease
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone past fifty is still on their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand for holding a painting or board.

clue.text: Prime Minister lets go and goes to pieces

indicators.note: going to pieces breaks up the words before it so they can be reassembled

explanation.surface: The PM loses his grip and falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to pieces' rearranges LETS GO AND. William Gladstone was a Victorian British Prime Minister four times.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladstone was a Prime Minister of the United Kingdom in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Article on foreign currency — about one no longer current

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the coin's name goes round the numeral

parts.note: the cent is a coin in many foreign currencies, such as the dollar or euro
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about some foreign coin turns out to be out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' simply places AN in front. 'about' puts the I (one) inside CENT, giving CIENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancient belongs to the distant past, so it is no longer current or modern.

clue.text: Stay on the large side after a fit

indicators.note: after means the piece named first comes later in the answer

parts.note: a prop is a stay or support
OS stands for outsize, the large size in clothing

explanation.surface: Someone holds firm on the heavy side after a seizure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' is the adjective, suitable, not a seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means appropriate or to the point, which is what fit means as an adjective.

clue.text: Announcer gets little credit and that is right

parts.note: CR is the short form of credit
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A broadcaster gets only a little praise, and rightly so.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was an official who announced news in public.

clue.text: Oriental feature about 8

indicators.note: about means going round, so the facial feature surrounds the writer

parts.note: an ear is a feature of the head
the answer to 8 down, the novelist

explanation.surface: A facial trait shared with a writer marks someone from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterner is a person from the East, as Oriental can mean.

clue.text: He believes he is entered in certain races

indicators.note: entered in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the TT, or Tourist Trophy, is a set of motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man with faith says he has been entered for some races.
explanation.definitionFit: A theist is a person who believes in God.

clue.text: A writer who could be quite uncompromising, note

parts.note: stern means strict and unyielding
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: An author who might be very strict makes a note.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century novelist, a writer.

clue.text: Transient arrangement needed right now

indicators.note: an arrangement sets the letters of the word before it in a new order

explanation.surface: Something fleeting needs to be sorted out immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: Instanter is an old legal word for immediately, at once.

clue.text: The subject of progeny

definitions.meaning: a topic or matter under discussion

explanation.surface: A discussion about the topic of children.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means both a matter for debate and, in legal language, offspring.

clue.text: Part a lush grassy slope, part a scree

indicators.note: the second 'part' tells us the answer is part of the words at the start of the clue

explanation.surface: A hillside is partly covered in lush grass and partly loose stones.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run through 'parT A LUSH'. The clue as a whole describes the slope, which is partly grassy and partly scree.
explanation.definitionFit: A talus is a slope, especially one at a cliff foot that may be grassed or covered in rock debris.

clue.text: Gentlemen of the press making cracks?

definitions.meaning: journalists who file stories for newspapers
a report is a loud bang, so whatever makes such cracks is jokingly one of these

explanation.surface: Journalists are cracking jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists are reporters, and a report is also an explosive noise like a gun's crack.

clue.text: Blame the salesman taking stroll

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to rove is to wander or roam about

explanation.surface: The travelling salesman gets blamed for going out on a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove is to scold or censure, much like to blame someone.

clue.text: Champions quiet workers

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet
artisans are skilled manual workers

explanation.surface: Advocates of silent craftsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Partisans are strong supporters, people who champion a cause.

clue.text: Flashback

parts.note: split in two, the word gives a flash, a very short moment, and back, meaning to support someone

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Flashback' as 'flash' and 'back': both mean the answer, a brief instant and a supporter's verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A second is a moment, as quick as a flash, and to second is to back a proposal.

clue.text: Providing tea for single companion

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
per means for each
one is single

explanation.surface: Laying on tea for an unmarried escort.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone is a companion who accompanies a young person for propriety.

clue.text: Daren't, maybe, get fiery

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters of the word before it could be put another way

explanation.surface: Someone who dares not act gets heated anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' reorders the letters of DAREN'T; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means burning with passion, which is what fiery suggests.

clue.text: Crush tribal leaders with large following

parts.note: the leading letters, the first two, of tribal
ample means large or plentiful

explanation.surface: Chiefs with a large following stamp down opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' here takes the first two letters of 'tribal'; 'following' places AMPLE after them.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to tread down and crush underfoot.

clue.text: A couple of beasts uniting could present a problem

parts.note: a nag is an old horse, one beast of the pair
a ram is a male sheep, the second beast

explanation.surface: Two animals mating might cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniting' just joins the two beasts after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A word puzzle made by rearranging letters is a kind of problem for the solver.

clue.text: Get-up that makes a sober individual rage

parts.note: TT means teetotal, someone who never drinks
ire is anger or rage

explanation.surface: An outfit that would make a teetotaller furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire is clothing, the same as a get-up or outfit.

clue.text: Mixed in among relevant matter

indicators.note: in tells us the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something confused buried among the pertinent material.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is aMONG RELevant; 'matter' rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A mongrel is of mixed breed, so the word can mean mixed.

clue.text: Have offspring and, inevitably, a mess!

definitions.meaning: an animal giving birth to several young at once

explanation.surface: Having young always leads to chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To litter is to give birth to a brood, and litter is also scattered rubbish.

clue.text: Traveller vandalising train without point

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled letters surround the point
vandalising wrecks the word train, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: a tine is a prong or point, as on a fork

explanation.surface: A tramp damages a railway carriage that has lost a sharp bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vandalising' turns TRAIN into IRANT, and 'without' puts it around TINE: I-TINE-RANT. 'without' does not mean minus here.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerant is a person who moves from place to place, a traveller.

clue.text: A consumer bearing with a change of rate

parts.note: E, for east, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: a change of the word that follows means its letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A shopper copes when the price is altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' is a compass point, E; 'with a change of' reorders RATE into ATER after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater consumes food, so is literally a consumer.

clue.text: The Spanish swimmer is like a little fairy

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
a fin is what a fish swims with, so jokingly a swimmer

explanation.surface: A Spanish swimmer is said to look like a pixie.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicate, like an elf or a little fairy.

clue.text: Guard for a malefactor

definitions.meaning: a barrier that protects or encloses
a receiver of stolen goods, himself a criminal

explanation.surface: A barrier put up for a wrongdoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a protective barrier and, in slang, a dealer in stolen property.

clue.text: Drink the health of a high-minded person?

definitions.meaning: to raise a glass in honour of someone
jokingly, someone held in high regard, as in the darling of the town

explanation.surface: Raising a glass to a person of lofty principles.
explanation.definitionFit: To toast is to drink someone's health, and a celebrated person is the toast of the town.

clue.text: Cleaner hiding joint she's stolen

indicators.note: hiding means one word holds another out of sight inside it

parts.note: purer means cleaner, freer from dirt
a loin is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady conceals a joint of meat she has pinched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a charwoman but is the comparative adjective. 'hiding' puts LOIN inside PURER.
explanation.definitionFit: A purloiner is one who steals, so she who has stolen is one.

clue.text: Book — something to fall back on

definitions.meaning: to book is to arrange in advance, as with a table
a store kept back for emergencies

explanation.surface: A book kept as a standby.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve is to book ahead, and a reserve is a supply held back.

clue.text: Recall a peer newly created by the sovereign

indicators.note: newly created means the letters are made into something fresh

parts.note: a sovereign was a pound coin, and L is the pound sign's abbreviation

explanation.surface: A monarch withdraws a peerage just granted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly created' rearranges A PEER into REPEA; L follows for the pound. A sovereign is an old British gold coin worth one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or recall it.
